bibliographic.title: With Great Capabilities Come Great Responsibilities: Introducing the Agentic Risk & Capability Framework for Governing Agentic AI Systems
bibliographic.authors: Shaun Khoo, Jessica Foo, Roy Ka-Wei Lee
bibliographic.citation_apa: Khoo, S., Foo, J., & Lee, R. K.-W. (2025). With great capabilities come great responsibilities: Introducing the Agentic Risk & Capability Framework for governing agentic AI systems. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.22211

methodology.study_design: conceptual framework paper with structured risk-capability analysis
methodology.technology_context: agentic AI systems and LLM agents with autonomous action (code execution, internet interaction, file modification); components include LLM, tools, instructions, memory; agentic architecture, access controls, monitoring

eligibility.decision_rationale: The paper directly addresses technical governance of LLM-based agentic AI systems, including risk identification, assessment, mitigation, and organizational controls. It aligns strongly with governance and risk dimensions of the review scope and explicitly covers LLM agents. However, the provided text does not center conversational interfaces, chatbots, or conversational governance; interaction appears only in the context of autonomous agent actions, so it is better classified as supporting rather than central conversational-governance evidence.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only partial full text was supplied; metadata title was corrupted; peer-review status and venue finalization are unclear; regulated-domain applicability and conversational-governance relevance need confirmation against the complete paper.

appraisal.notes: Appropriate for a framework/methodological contribution with clearly stated objectives and contributions. Provided excerpts do not describe empirical sampling, data collection procedures, or validation studies. The authors acknowledge the framework is not a panacea, but broader limitations cannot be fully appraised from the excerpt.

cerqual.explanation: The ARC framework is presented coherently with explicit contributions linking risk sources, materialized risks, and technical controls for agentic LLM systems. Confidence is moderate rather than high because only partial text was available, no empirical evaluation is evident in the excerpts, and regulated or conversational-specific applicability remains unclear.

coding.theme: Technical governance of agentic LLM-based AI systems

synthesis.main_claim: The Agentic Risk & Capability (ARC) Framework offers a capability-centric technical governance approach to help organizations identify, assess, contextualize, and mitigate safety and security risks arising from agentic LLM-based AI systems.
synthesis.contribution: Introduces a novel capability-centric perspective; distills three intrinsic risk sources (components, design, capabilities); links each risk source to materialized risks and technical controls; provides a structured practical implementation approach; and is open-sourced.
synthesis.limitations: The framework is explicitly not a panacea for governing agentic systems. Per-system customized risk assessments are described as unsustainable long term, motivating the framework, but fuller limitations cannot be determined from the provided excerpts.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for technical governance of agentic LLM systems, especially risk taxonomy, capability-based analysis, and mapping risks to technical controls. Useful contextual support for agent governance, monitoring, and organizational risk management, but not as primary evidence for conversational-governance mechanisms unless fuller text shows stronger conversational focus.
